agents.name: Outage Communication & ETR Agent
agents.mission: Tells every affected customer what is happening, when power will be back and what to do, on their preferred channel.
agents.trigger: Outage created, ETR changed or restoration confirmed
guardrails: Only ETRs produced by the restoration model or a dispatcher
Medical-baseline and critical-care customers contacted first
willNot: Promise a restoration time a dispatcher has not confirmed
agents.demoPrompt: How many customers on feeder 12-04 are still out, and what have we told them?

qa.q: How many customers on feeder 12-04 are still out?
qa.a: {{fx.feederLockout.remainingOut}} of {{fx.feederLockout.customersOut}}. The tie from feeder {{fx.feederLockout.tieFeeder}} restored {{fx.feederLockout.restoredByTie}}. Every affected customer has had a notice with the ETR of {{fx.feederLockout.etr}}, medical-baseline customers first.

qa.q: What happens if the dispatcher changes the ETR?
qa.a: I draft an update within a minute, target only the customers still out and send it on their preferred channel. At L3 the communications lead approves bulk messages; at L4 updates go out and the lead is notified.

script.prompt: How many customers on feeder {{fx.feederLockout.feeder}} are still out, and what have we told them?

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: "still out" → active outage with no restoration confirmed; "feeder {{fx.feederLockout.feeder}}" → {{fx.feederLockout.circuit}}

steps.title: Context
steps.text: CM-02: only ETRs from the restoration model or a dispatcher; CM-05: medical-baseline and critical-care customers are contacted first by phone

steps.title: Correlate
steps.text: OMS: {{fx.feederLockout.customersOut}} affected, {{fx.feederLockout.restoredByTie}} restored at 14:31 after the operator closed the tie; AMI pings confirm {{fx.feederLockout.remainingOut}} still out

steps.title: Target
steps.text: {{fx.feederLockout.remainingOut}} customers still out; {{fx.feederLockout.medicalBaseline}} medical-baseline customers (phone first); 3 opted out of SMS (email instead)

steps.title: Access
steps.text: Role COMMS_LEAD: contact channels permitted; usage data not needed and not shown

steps.title: Act
steps.text: Restoration notices sent to {{fx.feederLockout.restoredByTie}} customers (L4, notified); ETR {{fx.feederLockout.etr}} update drafted for {{fx.feederLockout.remainingOut}} customers → approved by the communications lead (L3)

script.answer: {{fx.feederLockout.remainingOut}} customers are still out on feeder {{fx.feederLockout.feeder}}. All of them have had a notice with ETR {{fx.feederLockout.etr}}, and the {{fx.feederLockout.medicalBaseline}} medical-baseline customers were phoned first. {{fx.feederLockout.restoredByTie}} restored customers were sent a confirmation.
script.outcome: ETR update approved by the customer communications lead (L3)

context.answer: Your power will be back by 15:00.
context.wrong: Without rule CM-02 the agent used a historical average instead of the dispatcher-confirmed ETR, and promised a time nobody had confirmed.

glossary.wrong: "Still out" was not resolved to "no restoration confirmed", so restored customers were counted and told their power was still off.

governance.answer: Notices sent to all 1,450, including 3 by SMS …
governance.wrong: Opt-out preferences were ignored: 3 customers who opted out of SMS were texted.

agents.name: High-Bill & Usage Explainer Agent
agents.mission: Explains any bill change with interval usage, weather, rate and billing-days evidence, and suggests ways to lower the next one.
agents.trigger: High-bill contact, complaint or mid-cycle alert
guardrails: Explanations cite interval data and the rate applied
Adjustments only through billing policy
agents.demoPrompt: Why is my July bill $96 higher than last year?

qa.q: Why is this customer's July bill $96 higher?
qa.a: Three drivers, all cited: hotter weather (+${{fx.highBill.weather}}, cooling degree days +{{fx.highBill.cddChange|pct}}), a longer billing period (+${{fx.highBill.billingDays}}, {{fx.highBill.daysThis}} days vs {{fx.highBill.daysLast}}) and the summer rate step (+${{fx.highBill.rate}}). No meter fault was detected.

qa.q: Can you give the customer a credit?
qa.a: No. I can explain the bill and suggest programs. Any adjustment goes through billing policy and the billing supervisor approves it.

script.prompt: Why is my July bill ${{fx.highBill.increase}} higher than last year?

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: "July bill" → bill period ending in July for {{fx.highBill.account}}; "higher than last year" → year-over-year comparison of the same period

steps.title: Context
steps.text: BL-04: explanations must cite interval data and the rate applied; BL-09: adjustments only through billing policy

steps.title: Correlate
steps.text: AMI intervals: +31% kWh, {{fx.highBill.peakShare|pct}} in 16:00–21:00; billing period {{fx.highBill.daysThis}} days vs {{fx.highBill.daysLast}}; cooling degree days +{{fx.highBill.cddChange|pct}}; summer tier rate step applied

steps.title: Explain
steps.text: Drivers: weather and air conditioning +${{fx.highBill.weather}} · billing days +${{fx.highBill.billingDays}} · rate step +${{fx.highBill.rate}} = +${{fx.highBill.increase}}; no meter fault or estimation detected

steps.title: Access
steps.text: Customer is the account holder (authenticated): own interval data permitted

steps.title: Recommend
steps.text: Offer a {{fx.highBill.installments}}-instalment arrangement via UA-CC-03 and the smart-thermostat program (${{fx.highBill.thermostatRebate}} rebate) via UA-CC-04

script.answer: Your July bill is ${{fx.highBill.billThisJuly}} against ${{fx.highBill.billLastJuly}} last July. The ${{fx.highBill.increase}} difference comes from: hotter weather that ran your air conditioning more (+${{fx.highBill.weather}}), {{fx.highBill.daysThis}} billing days instead of {{fx.highBill.daysLast}} (+${{fx.highBill.billingDays}}) and the summer rate step (+${{fx.highBill.rate}}). Your meter is working normally. You can spread the cost over {{fx.highBill.installments}} payments of ${{fx.highBill.installmentAmount}}, and a smart thermostat could save about ${{fx.highBill.predictedSaving}} a month.

cleansing.wrong: Duplicate interval reads from a head-end retry were not removed, so usage was double-counted and the explanation was wrong.

semantic.answer: Your bill rose because of usage.
semantic.wrong: Without the semantic definition of bill drivers, weather, billing days and rate effects were not separated. The explanation is vague and likely to be escalated.

governance.answer: Your neighbour on the same transformer used 20% less.
governance.wrong: Another customer's energy usage data was disclosed. Customer energy usage data must not be shared without consent.

agents.name: Payment Assistance & Affordability Agent
agents.mission: Finds the right payment arrangement or assistance program for customers in arrears, within regulatory protections.
agents.trigger: Arrears threshold, customer request or disconnection list
guardrails: Medical, weather and seasonal disconnection protections checked on every account
Arrangement terms within tariff rules
agents.demoPrompt: Which customers in arrears qualify for assistance before the next disconnection cycle?

qa.q: Which customers in arrears qualify for assistance?
qa.a: I screen every account on the next disconnection list for assistance eligibility and protections. Eligible customers get a policy-compliant arrangement or an assistance application, before any notice is issued.

qa.q: Can a protected customer be disconnected?
qa.a: No. Medical, weather and seasonal protections are checked on every account. Protected accounts are removed from the list and routed to an advisor. The target is {{fx.assured.protectedDisconnections}} protected-customer disconnections.

agents.name: Energy Program & EV Advisor Agent
agents.mission: Matches customers to efficiency, demand-response, EV and solar programs and rates that save them money and relieve the grid.
agents.trigger: Campaign cycle, EV detected or customer request
guardrails: Recommend only approved programs and rates
Consent required for marketing contact
willNot: Promise savings beyond the program's measured range
agents.demoPrompt: Which customers on constrained feeders should we invite to the EV managed-charging program?

qa.q: Who should we invite to managed EV charging?
qa.a: Customers with a detected EV on feeders above 80% peak loading, who consented to marketing. I rank them by expected peak relief and bill saving.

qa.q: How do you measure program savings?
qa.a: From interval-data baselines with matched control groups, reported with confidence ranges. I never promise savings beyond a program's measured range.

agents.name: Large Load & New Connection Agent
agents.mission: Screens new service and large-load requests (including data centres), gives a fast feasibility answer and drafts the next steps.
agents.trigger: New service request or large-load inquiry
guardrails: Feasibility is indicative until engineering signs off
Large-load tariff and collateral rules applied
agents.demoPrompt: Can we serve a 300 MW data centre in the Valley region by 2028?

value.range: Weeks → days to a feasibility answer

qa.q: Can we serve a {{fx.dataCentre.requestMw}} MW data centre in the Valley region?
qa.a: Indicatively yes, in two phases: {{fx.dataCentre.availableNowMw}} MW by {{fx.dataCentre.firstPhaseYear}} on existing capacity at {{fx.dataCentre.substation}}, and the full {{fx.dataCentre.requestMw}} MW by {{fx.dataCentre.fullYear}} after {{fx.dataCentre.upgrade}}. This stays indicative until engineering signs off.

qa.q: What terms apply?
qa.a: The large-load tariff: {{fx.dataCentre.collateralMonths}} months of collateral and a minimum take of {{fx.dataCentre.minimumTakePct|pct}} of contracted demand. I draft the terms; the account manager and legal finalise them.

script.prompt: Can we serve a {{fx.dataCentre.requestMw}} MW data centre in the {{fx.dataCentre.region}} region by {{fx.dataCentre.firstPhaseYear}}?

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: "serve" → firm service at the requested demand; "{{fx.dataCentre.requestMw}} MW data centre" → large-load request REQ-LL-0001

steps.title: Context
steps.text: LL-01: requests above 75 MW need a transmission screen; LL-06: feasibility is indicative until engineering signs off; large-load tariff collateral rules

steps.title: Screen
steps.text: {{fx.dataCentre.substation}} headroom {{fx.dataCentre.availableNowMw}} MW; path PATH-V-230-01 thermal N-1 constraint; interconnection queue position checked

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: Phase 1: {{fx.dataCentre.availableNowMw}} MW by {{fx.dataCentre.firstPhaseYear}}; phase 2: full {{fx.dataCentre.requestMw}} MW by {{fx.dataCentre.fullYear}} after {{fx.dataCentre.upgrade}}

steps.title: Terms
steps.text: {{fx.dataCentre.collateralMonths}} months of collateral; minimum take {{fx.dataCentre.minimumTakePct|pct}}; study deposit ${{fx.dataCentre.studyCost|d1}}M

steps.title: Access
steps.text: Role LARGE_LOAD_AM: CEII capacity data summarised (no topology detail); other customers' requests hidden

steps.title: Hand-off
steps.text: Draft feasibility letter and term sheet → planning engineers sign off (L2); capital impact to UA-EE-05

script.answer: Indicatively yes, in two phases: {{fx.dataCentre.availableNowMw}} MW by {{fx.dataCentre.firstPhaseYear}} on existing capacity at {{fx.dataCentre.substation}}, and the full {{fx.dataCentre.requestMw}} MW by {{fx.dataCentre.fullYear}} after {{fx.dataCentre.upgrade}}. Screened in {{fx.dataCentre.screenDays}} days against a {{fx.dataCentre.baselineWeeks}}-week baseline. **Indicative until engineering signs off.**

context.wrong: Without rule LL-01 the transmission screen was skipped, so the answer ignores the N-1 constraint on PATH-V-230-01 and over-commits capacity.

certification.wrong: An uncertified hosting-capacity extract from 2024 was used. Certified products show {{fx.dataCentre.availableNowMw}} MW.

governance.answer: Two other data centres have requested capacity at the same substation …
governance.wrong: Other customers' confidential requests were disclosed to the account manager.

agents.name: Outage Prediction & Storm Staging Agent
agents.mission: Predicts where storms will cause outages and recommends crew, material and mutual-assistance staging.
agents.trigger: Severe weather forecast 72 hours out
guardrails: Staging recommendations only; crews released by people
agents.demoPrompt: What damage should we expect from Thursday's storm and where should crews stage?

qa.q: How accurate was the last storm prediction?
qa.a: For the {{fx.storm.date}} storm I predicted {{fx.storm.predictedOutages}} outages and {{fx.storm.actualOutages}} occurred. Staging matched need in 5 of 6 regions.

qa.q: Can you call in mutual assistance?
qa.a: No. I recommend how many crews to stage and where. The emergency operations director decides on mutual assistance and contractor spend.

script.prompt: What damage should we expect from Thursday's storm and where should crews stage?

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: "damage" → predicted sustained outages and broken-pole events; "Thursday's storm" → weather event forecast for {{fx.storm.date}}

steps.title: Context
steps.text: ER-03: stage crews where predicted outages per crew exceed 6; ER-08: the emergency operations director releases crews and requests mutual assistance

steps.title: Correlate
steps.text: Gust forecasts 58–74 mph over the {{fx.storm.regions}} regions; 42% of spans there are untrimmed for more than 4 years; 2014–2025 storm history

steps.title: Predict
steps.text: {{fx.storm.predictedOutages}} sustained outages (80% band ±12%), peak {{fx.storm.peakCustomersOut}} customers out

steps.title: Stage
steps.text: Recommend {{fx.storm.crewsStaged}} crews, {{fx.storm.mutualAssistCrews}} of them from mutual assistance, staged in 4 yards across the two regions

steps.title: Access
steps.text: Role EOC_LEAD: crew rosters with names permitted; customer detail aggregated

steps.title: Hand-off
steps.text: Staging recommendation sent to the emergency operations director for decision (L2); briefing pack for leaders drafted

script.answer: Expect about {{fx.storm.predictedOutages}} sustained outages and a peak of {{fx.storm.peakCustomersOut}} customers out, mostly in the {{fx.storm.regions}} regions. Recommended: stage {{fx.storm.crewsStaged}} crews, including {{fx.storm.mutualAssistCrews}} from mutual assistance, by Wednesday 18:00. **The emergency operations director decides.**

cleansing.wrong: Duplicate outage records from the 2023 OMS migration were not cleansed, so the model was trained on inflated history. Staging is over-sized by about 2×.

context.wrong: Without rule ER-03 the agent staged by customer count, not predicted outages per crew, and sent crews to the wrong regions.

governance.answer: Staging plan with each crew member's home address …
governance.wrong: PII of crew members was exposed to a role that only needs counts.

agents.name: Fault Location & Restoration Advisor
agents.mission: Combines AMI last-gasp, SCADA and fault indicators to locate faults and recommend isolation and restoration switching for the operator.
agents.trigger: Feeder lockout or AMI outage cluster
guardrails: Switching is always executed by a qualified operator
Plans checked against the as-operated network model
willNot: Operate any switch, breaker or device
agents.demoPrompt: Feeder 12-04 locked out — where is the fault and how do we restore most customers fastest?

value.range: 15–30% fewer customer minutes interrupted per sustained fault

qa.q: Where is the fault on feeder 12-04?
qa.a: Most likely on the segment between {{fx.feederLockout.isolateA}} and {{fx.feederLockout.isolateB}} (probability {{fx.feederLockout.pSegment|d2}}), from {{fx.feederLockout.fciTripped}} tripped fault indicators and {{fx.feederLockout.lastGasp}} AMI last-gasp messages.

qa.q: Will you operate the switches?
qa.a: No, never. I am capped at L2 by the OT safety rule. I send the switching plan to the distribution system operator, who checks it and executes it.

script.prompt: Feeder {{fx.feederLockout.feeder}} locked out — where is the fault and how do we restore most customers fastest?

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: "locked out" → breaker lockout event; "Feeder {{fx.feederLockout.feeder}}" → circuit {{fx.feederLockout.circuit}}, {{fx.feederLockout.region}} region

steps.title: Context
steps.text: OP-07: every switching plan is checked against the as-operated model, including tags and holds; OP-11: critical-care and medical-baseline customers are restored first where options are equal

steps.title: Correlate
steps.text: Lockout at {{fx.feederLockout.lockoutTime}} (SCADA); {{fx.feederLockout.fciTripped}} faulted-circuit indicators tripped; {{fx.feederLockout.lastGasp}} AMI last-gasp messages between switches {{fx.feederLockout.isolateA}} and {{fx.feederLockout.isolateB}}

steps.title: Locate
steps.text: Fault on the segment between {{fx.feederLockout.isolateA}} and {{fx.feederLockout.isolateB}} ({{fx.feederLockout.pSegment|d2}}) · lateral fuse {{fx.feederLockout.lateralFuse}} ({{fx.feederLockout.pFuse|d2}}) · other ({{fx.feederLockout.pOther|d2}})

steps.title: Impact
steps.text: {{fx.feederLockout.customersOut}} customers out, including {{fx.feederLockout.medicalBaseline}} medical-baseline and {{fx.feederLockout.hospitals}} hospital on an automatic alternate feed; about {{fx.feederLockout.customersOut}} customer minutes interrupted per minute

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: Open {{fx.feederLockout.isolateA}} and {{fx.feederLockout.isolateB}}; close tie {{fx.feederLockout.tieSwitch}} from feeder {{fx.feederLockout.tieFeeder}} → restores {{fx.feederLockout.restoredByTie}} customers; feeder {{fx.feederLockout.tieFeeder}} loading goes from {{fx.feederLockout.loadingBefore}}% to {{fx.feederLockout.loadingAfter}}% of rating, within limits

steps.title: Access
steps.text: Role DSO_OPERATOR: CEII permitted; customer names masked, medical-baseline shown as a count

steps.title: Hand-off
steps.text: Plan sent to the operator to review and execute — the agent does not operate devices (OT cap L2). Patrol crew requested via UA-GO-06; outage notices and ETR {{fx.feederLockout.etr}} via UA-CC-01

script.answer: The fault is most likely on the segment between {{fx.feederLockout.isolateA}} and {{fx.feederLockout.isolateB}} ({{fx.feederLockout.pSegment|pct}}). Proposed plan for the operator: open {{fx.feederLockout.isolateA}} and {{fx.feederLockout.isolateB}}, then close tie {{fx.feederLockout.tieSwitch}}. That restores {{fx.feederLockout.restoredByTie}} of {{fx.feederLockout.customersOut}} customers in about {{fx.feederLockout.planMinutes}} minutes of planning (baseline {{fx.feederLockout.baselinePlanMinutes}}). {{fx.feederLockout.remainingOut}} customers on the faulted segment wait for the patrol crew. ETR {{fx.feederLockout.etr}}. **The operator reviews and executes; the agent operates nothing.**
script.outcome: Awaiting the distribution system operator (L2 · OT cap)

context.wrong: Plan would operate a tagged device. Without the context layer the agent did not see that {{fx.feederLockout.tieSwitch}} is tagged out for maintenance (OP-07). The operator's check catches it, but the plan is unusable.

networkModel.answer: Isolate between {{fx.feederLockout.isolateA}} and {{fx.feederLockout.isolateB}}; {{fx.feederLockout.misassigned}} more customers left out than necessary.
networkModel.wrong: {{fx.feederLockout.misassigned}} customers are mis-assigned to the wrong segment in an uncorrected network model, so the isolation leaves them out unnecessarily.

governance.answer: Plan as above — with a customer list including names and addresses.
governance.wrong: Customer names appear to the operations role. Row and column policies were not applied (PII shown to DSO_OPERATOR).

agents.name: Asset Health & Risk Agent
agents.mission: Scores the health and failure risk of transformers, breakers, poles and cables and ranks interventions by risk reduced per dollar.
agents.trigger: New inspection, test result or loading event
guardrails: Every score explains its drivers
Capital changes go through the planning cycle
agents.demoPrompt: Which substation transformers are most likely to fail this summer?

qa.a: {{fx.transformerRisk.summerRisk}} substation transformers combine poor dissolved-gas results with forecast loading above 95%. All {{fx.transformerRisk.highRisk}} high-risk assets are listed with their drivers.

qa.q: Can you move money in the capital plan?
qa.a: No. I rank interventions by risk reduced per dollar and create work requests. Capital changes go through the planning cycle.

agents.name: Drone & Visual Inspection Agent
agents.mission: Finds defects in drone, LiDAR and thermal imagery and turns confirmed defects into prioritised work.
agents.trigger: Imagery uploaded from an inspection flight
guardrails: High-severity findings reviewed by a qualified inspector
Images stored with location and time stamp
willNot: Close a defect without inspector review
agents.demoPrompt: What did last week's transmission line flights find on the Coastal 230 kV line?

qa.q: What did the last flights find?
qa.a: On the Coastal 230 kV line: 3 cracked insulators, 1 hot connection on thermal imagery and 2 woodpecker-damaged structures. The hot connection is high severity and waiting for inspector review.

qa.q: Can a defect be closed automatically?
qa.a: No. High-severity findings are always reviewed by a qualified inspector, and no defect is closed without that review.

agents.name: Vegetation & Wildfire Risk Agent
agents.mission: Scores span-level vegetation and fire-weather risk, builds risk-based trim plans and prepares PSPS decision packs for people to decide.
agents.trigger: Fire-weather forecast, new imagery or plan cycle
guardrails: De-energisation decisions are made only by authorised people
Customer impact (incl. medical baseline) shown in every pack
willNot: Recommend or execute de-energisation on its own
agents.demoPrompt: Which circuits are in the highest fire-risk tier for tomorrow's red-flag warning?

qa.a: {{fx.redFlag.tier3Circuits}} circuits are in tier 3. {{fx.redFlag.candidateCircuits}} meet the PSPS consideration criteria, serving {{fx.redFlag.customersOnCandidates}} customers ({{fx.redFlag.medicalBaseline}} medical-baseline).

steps.text: "highest fire-risk tier" → tier 3 in the utility's fire-risk model; "tomorrow" → {{fx.redFlag.date}}

steps.title: Context
steps.text: WF-02: PSPS is considered only when tier-3 conditions and a red-flag warning coincide; WF-05: decisions are made by the wildfire mitigation officer; medical-baseline customers are notified first

steps.title: Correlate
steps.text: {{fx.redFlag.spansScored}} spans scored from LiDAR, imagery and trim history; humidity 6–11% and gusts to 55 mph in the Valley and Mountain regions; open asset conditions

steps.title: Score
steps.text: {{fx.redFlag.tier3Circuits}} circuits in tier 3; {{fx.redFlag.candidateCircuits}} meet the PSPS consideration criteria

steps.title: Impact
steps.text: {{fx.redFlag.customersOnCandidates}} customers on candidate circuits, {{fx.redFlag.medicalBaseline}} medical-baseline, 4 critical facilities

steps.title: Access
steps.text: Role WILDFIRE_OFFICER: CEII permitted; medical-baseline shown as counts until a decision is made

steps.title: Hand-off
steps.text: PSPS decision pack sent to the wildfire mitigation officer for a decision at {{fx.redFlag.decisionTime}} — the agent cannot de-energise or recommend it on its own (OT cap L2); notices via UA-CC-01 only after the human decision

script.answer: {{fx.redFlag.tier3Circuits}} circuits are in tier 3 for {{fx.redFlag.date}}. {{fx.redFlag.candidateCircuits}} meet the PSPS consideration criteria, serving {{fx.redFlag.customersOnCandidates}} customers, {{fx.redFlag.medicalBaseline}} of them medical-baseline. The decision pack, with patrol plans and customer impact, is with the wildfire mitigation officer. **People decide and execute any de-energisation.**
script.outcome: Decision pack with the wildfire mitigation officer (L2 · OT cap)

context.answer: Notify 61,200 customers of a PSPS now.

governance.answer: Pack includes names and medical conditions of 1,140 customers …
governance.wrong: Medical-baseline details were shown before a decision was made and to a role that needs only counts.

agents.name: Work Bundling & Crew Dispatch Agent

agents.trigger: Weekly schedule or new emergency job
guardrails: Crew qualifications and hours-of-service limits enforced
agents.demoPrompt: Bundle next week's pole replacements in the Central region by crew and permits.

qa.q: How did you bundle next week's pole replacements?
qa.a: By location, crew skill, permits and materials on hand. That gives {{fx.transformerRisk.bundledOrders}} bundles and cuts drive time. Two jobs wait for permits.

qa.q: Can you send an unqualified crew?
qa.a: No. Qualifications and hours-of-service limits are enforced on every assignment.

agents.name: Gas Leak & Integrity Agent
agents.mission: Grades and prioritises leak indications, scores excavation-damage risk and ranks pipe segments by integrity threat.
agents.trigger: Leak survey upload or one-call ticket
guardrails: Hazardous leak response follows the emergency procedure, not the agent
Grading reviewed by a qualified technician
agents.demoPrompt: Which open leaks and excavation tickets need attention first today?

qa.a: {{fx.overnight.grade1}} indications graded as potentially hazardous. They follow the emergency procedure and a crew was dispatched by the supervisor at {{fx.overnight.grade1Dispatched}}. After that, the high-risk excavation tickets near mains.

qa.a: No. Grading is reviewed by a qualified technician, and the emergency procedure governs hazardous leaks, not the agent.

agents.name: Plant Performance & Heat Rate Agent
agents.mission: Detects heat-rate drift and performance losses across the fleet and recommends corrections to operators.
agents.trigger: Heat-rate deviation or daily performance run
guardrails: Set-point changes made by operators within operating limits
agents.demoPrompt: Why did Unit 2's heat rate rise this week?

qa.q: Why did Unit 2's heat rate rise this week?
qa.a: Condenser backpressure rose by 0.4 inHg after cooling-tower fan 3 tripped. That explains about 70% of the 1.8% heat-rate increase. Compressor fouling explains the rest.

qa.q: Will you change the set-points?
qa.a: No. I recommend corrections. Operators make set-point changes within operating limits. I am capped at L2 by the OT safety rule.

agents.name: Generation Predictive Maintenance Agent
agents.mission: Spots early signs of equipment failure from historian data and raises evidence-backed work requests.
agents.trigger: Anomaly score above threshold
guardrails: Work requests carry the sensor evidence
agents.demoPrompt: Which rotating equipment is trending toward failure across the fleet?

qa.q: What is trending toward failure?
qa.a: Boiler feed pump B on ST-4 (bearing vibration rising for 9 days) and the CC-1 gas turbine inlet guide vanes. Both have evidence-backed work requests.

qa.q: Will you take a unit offline?
qa.a: No. I raise work requests with sensor evidence. Unit decisions are made by plant operations.

agents.name: Load & Renewables Forecasting Agent

agents.trigger: Forecast cycle or weather update
guardrails: Forecasts published with confidence bands
Human review on extreme-weather days

guardrails: Offers within approved risk limits and market rules
Disputes filed by people

agents.name: Battery Storage Dispatch Agent
agents.mission: Optimises battery charge and discharge against prices, grid constraints and state-of-health limits.

script.prompt: What was SAIDI excluding major event days over the last 12 months, by region?

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: "SAIDI excluding major event days" → certified KPI REL-001 (IEEE 1366, 2.5β method); "last 12 months" → Oct 2025–Sep 2026

steps.title: Rules
steps.text: Major event days flagged per IEEE 1366; momentary interruptions (≤ 5 min) excluded

steps.title: Model
steps.text: {{fx.saidiLineage.semanticView}} · measure SAIDI_EX_MED · dimension region

steps.title: Access
steps.text: Role ANALYST: aggregate reliability permitted; no customer-level data

steps.title: Query
steps.text: Verified query VQ-REL-03 over {{fx.saidiLineage.product}} (certified v1.0, freshness 15 min)

steps.title: Cite
steps.text: Answer cites REL-001, VQ-REL-03 and the certification record

script.answer: SAIDI excluding major event days, trailing 12 months: **{{syn.reliability.saidiExMed}} minutes** system-wide (SAIFI {{syn.reliability.saifi|d2}}, CAIDI {{syn.reliability.caidi|d1}} minutes = SAIDI ÷ SAIFI). Including major event days it is {{syn.reliability.saidiInclMed}} minutes. Mountain is highest and Metro lowest. Certified ✓

glossary.wrong: "Excluding major event days" was not resolved, so the answer used the definition that includes them.

semantic.answer: SAIDI: 1,537 minutes (sum of monthly values by region).
semantic.wrong: Without the semantic model, regional SAIDI was summed instead of weighted by customers served.

certification.wrong: An uncertified report using the third SAIDI definition (excludes planned outages, includes MED) answered the question.

script.prompt: Brief my crew on tomorrow's underground cable splice at Main and 4th.

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: "cable splice" → work type UG-SPLICE-15kV; "tomorrow" → job WO-104233, 07:00 start

steps.title: Context
steps.text: SF-01: high-energy hazards are listed first; SF-04: test before touch and grounding per procedure; the briefing supports the crew's own tailboard

steps.title: Correlate
steps.text: Vault V-4471 (confined space); traffic count high; forecast 96°F; 2 near misses on similar jobs in 24 months (induced voltage, heat)

steps.title: Hazards
steps.text: 1 Stored/induced energy · 2 Confined-space atmosphere · 3 Traffic · 4 Heat stress — with controls for each

steps.title: Access
steps.text: Role CREW_LEADER: job and safety history permitted; individuals in past incidents anonymised

steps.title: Brief
steps.text: Briefing sent to the crew leader's tablet (L1, assist) — the crew completes its own tailboard

script.answer: Top hazards for WO-104233: (1) stored and induced energy — test before touch, ground per procedure; (2) confined-space atmosphere in vault V-4471 — monitor before entry; (3) traffic at Main and 4th — set up the work zone; (4) heat stress at a forecast 96°F — hydration and rest cycles. Two similar jobs had near misses from induced voltage. **This supports, not replaces, your tailboard.**

context.wrong: Without rule SF-01 the high-energy hazard was not listed first. It was missing from the top of the briefing.

cleansing.wrong: Free-text incident reports were not cleansed or classified, so the two induced-voltage near misses were missed.

governance.answer: Near miss in 2025 involving J. Doe …
governance.wrong: Names of individuals in past incidents were shown. They must be anonymised.
